tagline: The lively capital of the north is a student city of bikes and canals, with the Martinitoren tower, the colourful Groninger Museum and buzzing nightlife.
overview: Groningen is the largest city in the northern Netherlands and one of its liveliest: about a quarter of its residents are students at the University of Groningen or the Hanze University. Medieval trade made it a rich Hanseatic city, and its Grote Markt is overlooked by the Martinitoren, a 97-metre church tower.

Groningen is famous for cycling. Since the 1970s cars have been kept out of the centre, so bikes rule the streets, and more trips are made by bike than in almost any other city in the world. Canals ring the old town, lined with houseboats.

The Groninger Museum, a colourful building on its own island opposite the station, shows art, design and fashion. The Prinsenhof garden, the Forum cultural centre with its rooftop views, and late-night bars make it easy to spend a few days.
